body.x: ROWAN, Inc., (CEO Solomon Han) participated in the 'Startup Zone' at the Eureka Park K-STARTUP integrated hall of 'CES 2023' in Las Vegas, USA from January 5 (Thursday) to 8 (Sunday, local time) for a total of 4 days.

The company has designed and developed personalized cognitive intervention content based on the results derived from collecting and analyzing brain cognitive function information. With active use of technologies representing the 4th Industrial Revolution, such as big data and artificial intelligence (AI), in the development of their own content, the startup aims at providing effective solutions to prevent dementia in the rapidly aging demographic around the world.

To this end, ROWAN pursues a future-oriented business that collaborates with organizations (e.g., medical institutions, life insurance providers) with needs to manage researcher data. The company also seeks to become a leader in the digital treatment of brain diseases to meet their organizational culture's main principle, which is to “Optimize Surroundings.”

At the exhibition, ROWAN presented its dementia prevention program Superbrain. It offers features that evaluate individual cognitive levels, recommend real-time learning content based on the results, and apply automated evaluation algorithm technology. In addition, artificial intelligence algorithms are embedded to predict the possibility of improving cognitive improvement indicators based on deep learning, providing cognitive intervention therapy and cognitive training content as personalized treatment curricula.

The effectiveness of Superbrain was previously demonstrated in a clinical trial of 152 subjects aged 60 years or older for about three years. In 2020, the Ministry of Health and Welfare published the results of a study using Superbrain, which demonstrated a significant cognitive improvement, as well as over 90% of retention rate and compliance to the protocol.

“As digital therapy requires medical device certification to enter the market, which takes time and money, we are currently aiming to target the U.S. market with a two-track strategy that encompasses digital therapy and non-medical devices,” a ROWAN representative explained. “To this end, we are looking for joint promotion and marketing partners for the U.S. local commercialization of our non-medical devices, Superbrain Wellness, and FDA certification advisors and collaborators for our medical device Superbrain Dex.”

“Based on the results of large-scale clinical studies using existing digital programs in the field of dementia, we also are preparing to obtain certification from the Ministry of Food and Drug Safety, the FDA, and the German DiGA,” the representative added. “Moreover, we have started developing products for the expansion of the new product line for conditions such as tinnitus and depression, and the technological advancement of existing products is underway as well.”

‘CES’ is the world’s biggest IT trade show and is a place where one can see the direction and trends of the appliance industry of the entire world. Hosted by the Consumer Technology Association (CTA), it is held annually in Las Vegas, USA in January. Having reported on CES for 17 consecutive years, AVING News started reporting news of CES to the entire world since 2006, and conducted ‘BEST OF CES’, which chose the most innovative product and technology, and ‘BEST OF MADE IN KOREA, which chose the best innovative company in Korea. In addition, it vividly relayed on-site issues in CES through ‘AVING LIVE’.

The K-STARTUP Joint Pavilion featured joint participation of institutions like the Korea Institute of Startup & Entrepreneurship Development, Seoul Business Agency, and Seoul Digital Foundation, as well as 51 Korean innovative companies, to enter the US market and discover global partners. In addition, university student supporters of CES 2023 chosen by each university (Kyunghee, Kookmin, Sogang, Chung-Ang) matched to participating companies based on their respective majors and fields of business.
